name: FY2013 PMMR Agency Performance Indicators
description:
This dataset contains agency performance indicators from the FY2013 Mayor's Management Report (PMMR), covering New York City government agencies. Each row represents a reported measure for a specific agency, indicator, and sub-indicator, with fields describing the indicator's name and sequence, the desired direction of performance, whether it is flagged as critical, the geography and measure type, and the fiscal year. Values are stored in a raw form alongside formatted versions for percentages, numbers, currency, time, and ratios, plus conditional formatting information.

The data can be used to track and compare agency performance across indicators, identify measures where performance is moving in the desired or undesired direction, and examine critical indicators. Analysts, researchers, and the public can use it to build dashboards, assess trends within FY2013, and evaluate how different agencies report and measure their services.

name: NYC Business Acceleration Businesses Served and Jobs Created
description:
This dataset lists businesses served by NYC Business Acceleration, a city program that helps small businesses open and operate, along with the number of employees at each establishment. Each row represents one business and includes its doing-business-as name, street address, ZIP code, and borough, plus a business sector, establishment category, and type of cuisine where applicable. It also records the number of employees and the establishment's actual opening date. The sample covers 5,000 rows across nine columns.

The data can be used to map where served businesses are located across the five boroughs, compare business sectors and establishment types, and examine opening dates over time. It supports analyses of job counts by neighborhood or industry, studies of the restaurant and food-service landscape through the cuisine field, and program reporting on the reach of business acceleration services. Community organizations, researchers, and policymakers could use it to identify concentrations of small businesses and target support, though it reflects only businesses that engaged with the program rather than all NYC businesses.

name: NYC Business Acceleration Businesses Served and Jobs Created

name: NYC Business Acceleration Businesses Served and Jobs Created
description:
This dataset contains records of businesses served by NYC Business Acceleration, a New York City program that supports small businesses in opening and operating. Each row represents one establishment and includes its doing-business-as name, street address, ZIP code, borough, business sector, establishment category, and cuisine type where applicable, along with the number of employees and the actual opening date. The sample covers 5,000 rows across nine columns, with most businesses concentrated in sectors such as accommodations and food, and many located in Manhattan, Queens, and Brooklyn. Some fields, particularly cuisine type, business sector, and employee count, have notable missing values.

The data can be used to track business openings over time, compare activity across boroughs and sectors, examine the mix of food and retail establishments, estimate jobs associated with new businesses, and assess the reach of city business support services. It is suited to economic development and small business analysis focused on local commercial activity in New York City.

name: Issued Licenses
description:
This dataset records issued business licenses, with one row per license and 31 columns covering license details, business identity, location, and geography. Key fields include the license number, business name and trade name, business category and license type, license status, creation and expiration dates, and a free-text detail field. Contact information is limited to a phone number. Each record also includes a structured address (building, street, unit, city, state, ZIP) along with administrative and geographic identifiers such as borough, community board, council district, BIN, BBL, neighborhood tabulation area, census block and tract, and latitude/longitude coordinates.

The data can be used to analyze the distribution of licensed businesses by category, type, and status; to map business locations across neighborhoods and districts; to track license issuance and expiration over time; and to join with census or property data for local economic and planning research. name: Issued Licenses
description:
This dataset records issued business licenses, with each row representing a single license tied to a business. It includes 31 columns covering license identifiers, business names and trade names, business category, license type and status, creation and expiration dates, and contact phone numbers. Location details are extensive, including street address, city, state, ZIP code, borough, community board, council district, and geographic identifiers such as BIN, BBL, NTA, census tract, latitude, and longitude. Some fields, such as trade name, unit and suite, and several location attributes, are missing for a large share of rows.

The data could support analyses of licensing activity by business category, location, and status; mapping of licensed businesses across neighborhoods and districts; tracking of license creation and renewal timelines; and studies of geographic concentration or gaps in licensing. It may also be useful for address verification, contact outreach, or building dashboards that monitor active and expiring licenses.

name: Issued Licenses
description:
This dataset contains records of issued business licenses, with each row representing a licensed business. It includes the license number, type, and status, along with creation and expiration dates, business category, business name, and trade name. Contact and location details are also provided, such as phone number, street address, city, state, ZIP code, borough, community board, council district, census tract, and latitude/longitude coordinates. Many location fields are only partially populated, and some columns, such as secondary street names and unit details, are mostly or entirely empty.

The data can be used to analyze the number and density of licensed businesses by neighborhood, track license issuance and expiration trends over time, compare business categories across geographic areas, and support economic development or urban planning research. It is also suitable for building maps and dashboards of commercial activity, though users should account for missing values in address and geographic fields.
